summary: Light station set aside at the southwestern tip of Point Roberts, WA in 1908; the present light stands on a skeletal tower in Lighthouse Marine Park.

structures.note: Pyramidal wood-frame tower, about 30 ft (9.1 m) from base to lantern, concrete foundation, lens lantern (USLHS). The Point Roberts Historical Society dates a wood-framed lighthouse to 1910 and says it was damaged in 1962 and replaced.

26 ft (8 m) square skeletal tower with a red-and-white checkerboard daymark (Lighthouse Directory). The sources read do not date its erection; the Historical Society says the navigation light seen today replaced the wooden lighthouse after 1962.

access.note: Lighthouse Marine Park, a Whatcom County park. The site is open; the tower is closed (Lighthouse Directory). The US Lighthouse Society lists the light as not open to the public. Point Roberts is reached by a 14-mile boat trip from Blaine or a drive through Canada (HistoryLink).

resolved_conflicts.field: history of the tower (1908 / 1910 / never built)
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The USLHS record gives a tower established in 1908 with a lens lantern. The Historical Society gives a wood-framed lighthouse built in 1910. HistoryLink and the Lighthouse Directory say no lighthouse was built. The 1918 Lighthouse Service Bulletin lists Point Roberts among illuminant changes, so a working light existed by 1918. The sources do not settle the construction date.

HistoryLink says Lighthouse Marine Park is named for a lighthouse that was never built. The Historical Society says it is named for the wood-framed lighthouse damaged in 1962. Both are stated in the story.
The Lighthouse Directory says active. The USLHS record says not an active aid to navigation. A tourism site says decommissioned. Not resolved; the story states the disagreement.

The record has 6.1 m. USLHS gives 25 ft (7.6 m) above mean high water. The Lighthouse Directory gives a focal plane of 30 ft (9 m). No source read gives 6.1 m. Left to the editor; the record's value is not changed here.
The record has Fl(2) W 5s (from the Light List, per the record). The Lighthouse Directory gives two white flashes every 15 s, which is Fl(2) W 15s. Not resolved by any source read.

notes_for_editor: Thin and conflicting. The only primary source is the 1918 Lighthouse Service Bulletin entry (PDF page 55) and the 1918-1923 index (p. 30, 'Point Roberts, change in illuminant 55'). The corpus holds no Lighthouse Board or Commissioner volume for 1908-1918 that names the station; the Commissioner's 1919 list mentions a 'Point Roberts' light, but the OCR is too garbled to quote. The Chronicling America search for Washington papers, 1906-1912, found nothing about the light (a 1909 Leavenworth Echo item concerns a boundary monument survey at Point Roberts). No keeper roster exists in the USLHS record, and it lists no keepers' quarters; whether the light was ever staffed is not stated in the sources read. The Historical Society's 1910 date, its 1962 storm damage and its 1973 park naming are from a single local article; they need a Coast Guard or Lighthouse Service primary record. The record's 'active' status and the USLHS 'Active Aid to Navigation: No' contradict each other; the record's Light List characteristic and focal height are not confirmed by any source read. Wikipedia (lead only, not cited) gives 25 ft (7.6 m) height, a focal height of 9 m, and two white flashes every 15 seconds. The USLHS record's coordinates are garbled ('48 97'', '123 08''); the roster tool's position is wrong and the record's 48.9716, -123.0837 agrees with the Wikipedia lead. The Life-Saving Service stranding tables list Point Roberts as a place of strandings from 1902 to 1909; the tables do not tie any wreck to the light, so none is recorded here. The USLHS record has a 1908 photograph credited to Josephine Aberg (not fetched; licence to be checked before any use). Fact-check 2026-10-28: all 36 quotes were found on the first run. Checked against the USLHS record, HistoryLink, the Lighthouse Directory (ibiblio), the All Point Bulletin article, Map of US and the 1918 Lighthouse Service Bulletin (PDF page 55). The Directory dates the present light 'Date unknown' and calls it Active; the story now states the Directory's 'active' reading beside the USLHS 'not active' reading. The 1918 Bulletin lists Point Roberts under 'Important changes in aids to navigation' (fixed to flashing, oil to acetylene), so a light was operating in 1918. The All Point Bulletin article calls the park a county park and says the lighthouse was built in 1910; the story gives both as the Historical Society's. Fixed in the text: the 'joined to Tsawwassen' clause (no source), the homesteading and Columbus Day paraphrases, the 'stood there until 1962' wording, the Whatcom County citation, the tower-closed citation, and 'a working light' (now 'a light was operating'). Two HistoryLink quotations were paraphrased so that one short quotation from that copyrighted site remains (unincorporated American exclave).
